native_result.query: At what Socioeconomic levels is the advantage in completion rates for Black students more pronounced?
native_result.HypoA: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students becomes more pronounced at higher SES levels indicated by a positive interaction term SES*is_Black(coefficient:0.6271 (significant))
native_result.HypoB: Black students show no unconditional completion advantage (Black below White in every SES quartile); the only data-supported Black advantage is conditional and interactive — Black BA-completion rises significantly faster with SES than White's (logistic BLACK x SES = +0.76, p~0.003), so the Black-White gap narrows monotonically with SES, crosses parity near SES ~ +1.0 to +1.3 (externally normed scale) and turns positive in the upper tail. The advantage is therefore most pronounced at upper-middle-to-high socioeconomic levels (~upper quartile, SES > +0.5; crossover +1.0-1.3), not at low SES, though the high-SES estimate is imprecise (small Black cells: 35 Black at SES>=1.5, 3 completions; CI includes parity across the whole SES range, excluding 0 only below SES~+0.7 where Black are significantly below White).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Load 8,773-row NLS SES file; drop stray index column; BA as binary. 2) Pooled-quartile strata: completion rate by race, percentage-point gaps Black minus White and Black minus all-others with Wald CIs (outputs/quartile_strata.csv). 3) Sensitivity: tertiles and fixed reference thresholds low<−0.5/mid/high>+0.5 (CSVs). 4) Univariable logistic BA ~ SES + race + SES×race (White ref); primary interaction test = BLACK×SES (coef +0.76, p=0.0028). 5) Headline deliverable: continuous-SES predicted Black−White pp-gap curve with delta-method 95% CI band (outputs/predicted_gap_curve.csv + .svg); crossover SES≈1.26; CI excludes 0 only below SES≈0.70. 6) Robustness: adjusted logistic adding sex, ASVAB z, percentile z (BLACK×SES +0.76, p=0.0057; crossover≈0).
